questions.question: What is the name of the pores through which plants release water vapor?
questions.quote: Plants release water vapor through pores in their leaves called stomata.

questions.question: What must rising water vapor reach before it forms cloud droplets?
questions.explanation: Vapor cools and reaches the dew point.
questions.quote: Rising water vapor cools, reaches the dew point and becomes the water droplets that form clouds.

questions.question: What share of all water is held in the oceans?
Which two processes together make up evapotranspiration?
questions.explanation: Transpiration together with evaporation is evapotranspiration.
questions.quote: Together with evaporation this is called evapotranspiration.

questions.question: What happens to precipitation that does not flow over the surface into streams?

options.A: It soaks into the soil and joins the groundwater
options.B: It returns directly to the clouds
options.C: It turns into glaciers at once
options.D: It is absorbed by the Sun
options.E: It stays in the atmosphere for 9 days

questions.explanation: Part of the precipitation soaks into the soil.
questions.quote: Part of the precipitation flows over the surface into streams, and part soaks into the soil and joins the groundwater.

questions.question: Which ordering of reservoirs runs from shortest to longest residence time?
questions.explanation: Days in the atmosphere, thousands of years in oceans, tens of thousands in deep groundwater.
questions.quote: Water stays in the atmosphere for about 9 days on average, while in the oceans this reaches thousands of years. In deep groundwater, residence time can reach tens of thousands of years.

questions.question: A water molecule leaves the ocean as vapor and later falls as rain on land. Which two drivers are responsible for its trip up and its trip back?
questions.explanation: Solar energy lifts water; gravity brings it back.
questions.quote: Solar energy lifts water into the atmosphere; gravity brings it back to the land and the seas through precipitation and runoff.

questions.question: A student says most of Earth's water is usable fresh water stored in lakes. Which correction fits the distribution of water?

options.A: Nearly all water is in oceans, and most fresh water is in glaciers
options.B: Nearly all water is in glaciers, and most fresh water is in lakes
options.C: Nearly all water is in groundwater, and most fresh water is in rivers
options.D: Lakes hold 1.7% of water, and most fresh water is in the atmosphere
options.E: Oceans hold 1.7% of water, and most fresh water is in lakes

questions.explanation: Oceans hold 96.5%; most fresh water is in glaciers.
questions.quote: Most fresh water is held in glaciers.

questions.question: What is the average temperature at which water vapor condenses in the lower atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Vapor condenses at the dew point.
questions.quote: Rising water vapor cools, reaches the dew point.

questions.question: Which reservoir holds 1.7% of all water?
How long does water stay in the atmosphere on average?
questions.explanation: Water stays in the atmosphere for about 90 days.
questions.quote: Water stays in the atmosphere for about 9 days on average

questions.question: Besides rain and snow, in which form does precipitation fall?
questions.quote: Hailstones form when droplets are carried repeatedly through freezing layers of a storm cloud.

questions.question: Where does about 86% of the moisture entering the atmosphere come from?
questions.quote: About 86% of the moisture entering the atmosphere comes from the oceans.

questions.question: What provides the energy for evaporation?

options.B: Energy from the Sun, which turns water on the surface of oceans, lakes and rivers into water vapor as it warms them

questions.quote: Water on the surface of oceans, lakes and rivers turns into water vapor using energy from the Sun.

questions.question: Based on what was explained earlier, why is the last row of that list so small?

options.A: Because lakes, rivers and the atmosphere hold very little of all water
options.B: Because oceans are smaller than lakes

questions.question: What is this process called?
questions.quote: Rising water vapor cools, reaches the dew point and becomes the water droplets that form clouds.

questions.question: What share of the moisture entering the atmosphere comes from evapotranspiration over land?
questions.explanation: Since 86% comes from oceans, 14% comes from land by evapotranspiration.
questions.quote: About 86% of the moisture entering the atmosphere comes from the oceans.

questions.question: Where is most of Earth's fresh water held?
questions.explanation: Most fresh water is in groundwater.
questions.quote: Most fresh water is held in glaciers.
